propositions: The three most recent successful full-route Gerrit Verify runs completed in 22m47s–26m14s with no individual pytest phase exceeding 30s, meeting the 20–30 minute completion objective.

A local exhaustive macOS census (1048.61s default, 114.68s integration) identified 501 unique ≥1.0s phases; CI logs expose only top 25 per invocation, creating measurement limitation for phases below that rank.
The previously reported 57m29s failure was job sequencing (25m13s admission + 30m23s own job) caused by missing !cancelled() dependency in Gerrit 1792, now fixed.

Gerrit 1817 merged 19 OS/Python-invariant repository-policy nodes from macOS/Ubuntu 3.11/3.12 into Ubuntu 3.13-only, expecting ~8s macOS wall and 24.84 aggregate runner-seconds with no new job/setup overhead.

All 501 inventoried phases at or above 1.0s have been classified into families (git-store, import-packaging, analyzer-grounding, gate-identity-signing, deploy-reviewbot, editor-e2e, pandoc, api-reconciler-schema, other-contract) with keep/research/refactor dispositions and coverage rationales.

Ranked next actions preserve real Git/process/filesystem/socket behavior while research on equivalence, fixture scaling, and test-window injection proceeds without adding runner jobs or pushing code changes.
